title: Claude Code Skills
one_liner: A skill is a folder containing SKILL.md. Its description decides when Claude loads it; its location decides who gets it.

core.title: A skill is a folder with a SKILL.md file
core.body: `SKILL.md` holds YAML frontmatter (when to use the skill) and markdown instructions (what to do). The directory name, or frontmatter `name`, becomes the `/command`. Detailed material goes in supporting files that `SKILL.md` links to, so it loads only when needed.
core.why: A short `SKILL.md` keeps context cost low; reference files and scripts carry the detail.

quotes.text: Keep `SKILL.md` under 500 lines. Move detailed reference material to separate files.
quotes.label: Skills > Add supporting files

core.title: The description is the trigger
core.body: Claude reads the `description` of each skill and uses it to decide whether to load the full skill. Put the key use case first and include words users would naturally say.
core.why: A vague description means the skill is not used automatically. Malformed YAML leaves the skill callable by `/name` but not matchable.

quotes.text: Check the description includes keywords users would naturally say
quotes.label: Skills > Troubleshooting

core.title: Location decides who gets the skill
core.body: Personal skills (`~/.claude/skills/`) apply to all your projects; project skills (`.claude/skills/`) apply to one repository and can be committed. Enterprise, nested, plugin and claude.ai account locations also exist. On a name clash, enterprise beats personal, and personal beats project.
core.why: Commit project skills to share them with the team; keep personal workflows in your home directory.

quotes.label: Skills > Choose where skills load

core.title: You can control who invokes a skill
core.body: `disable-model-invocation: true` makes a skill manual only; use it for side effects such as deploy or commit. `user-invocable: false` makes it background knowledge that only Claude can invoke.
core.why: Otherwise Claude may start a workflow with side effects when it judges the moment suitable.

quotes.text: Claude can't invoke the skill on its own.
quotes.label: Skills > Control who invokes a skill

quotes.text: Only Claude can invoke the skill.
quotes.label: Skills > Control who invokes a skill

core.title: Invoked skill content stays in context
core.body: Once invoked, the rendered content stays in the conversation as one message and is not re-read from disk. After compaction, only the first 5,000 tokens of each skill are kept.
core.why: Every line has a recurring token cost. Write guidance that applies to the whole task and put the most important instructions first.

quotes.text: keeping the first 5,000 tokens of each
quotes.label: Skills > Skill content lifecycle

quotes.text: every line is a recurring token cost
quotes.label: Skills > Types of skill content

core.title: Dynamic context and forked subagents
core.body: A line such as `!`git diff HEAD`` is replaced with the command output before Claude reads the skill. `context: fork` runs the skill in a separate subagent that has no access to the conversation history.
core.why: Injected commands give Claude live data instead of guesses. Forked skills must be self-contained.

quotes.text: Claude Code runs the command and replaces the line with its output before Claude sees the skill content
quotes.label: Skills > Create your first skill

quotes.text: The subagent doesn't see your conversation history, so the skill's instructions have to stand on their own.
quotes.label: Skills > Run skills in a subagent

practice.title: Create a skill that injects live context
practice.goal: Observe automatic loading and dynamic context injection in one skill.
steps: In a git repository with uncommitted changes, ask Claude what changed. Then run `/summarize-changes` directly.

code.text:
---
description: Summarizes uncommitted changes and flags anything risky. Use when the user asks what changed, wants a commit message, or asks to review their diff.
---

## Current changes

!`git diff HEAD`

## Instructions

Summarize the changes above in two or three bullet points, then list any risks you notice.

practice.check: Claude summarizes your actual diff without you pasting it, in both cases.
practice.variation: Replace the description with a vague one, such as 'helps with code', and test whether it still loads automatically.

practice.title: Make a skill manual only
steps: Create `.claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md` with a short `description` and `disable-model-invocation: true`
Ask Claude in plain language to deploy
practice.check: Claude does not run the skill on its own, but runs it when you type the command.
practice.variation: Change the field to `user-invocable: false` and confirm the `/deploy` command is no longer available to you.

practice.title: Move detail into a supporting file
steps: Add `reference.md` to the skill folder from exercise 1 with a list of risk categories
In `SKILL.md`, add a line: `For risk categories, see [reference.md](reference.md)`
practice.check: Claude's risk list reflects the categories in `reference.md`.
practice.variation: Remove the link from `SKILL.md` and compare the result.

gotchas: Frontmatter only counts when the opening `---` is the first line of the file. Otherwise the markers become skill content.
Unrecognized frontmatter field names are ignored without an error. Match the field names exactly, hyphens included.
After compaction, only the start of a skill is kept. Re-invoke the skill, or move rules that must always hold into a hook.
An `allowed-tools` grant clears when you send your next message, although the skill content remains.

recall.q: What does Claude use to decide whether to load a skill automatically?
The same skill name exists in personal and project locations. Which runs?
How do you prevent Claude from running a deploy skill by itself?
Where should large reference material go?
recall.a: In supporting files linked from `SKILL.md`, which should stay under 500 lines.

recall.q: Why might Claude stop following a skill late in a session?
recall.a: The content is not re-read each turn, and compaction keeps only the start. Re-invoke it or use a hook.
